title: the artifact journal keeps the newest entry per path in the repo and every entry in a day trail under ~/.cairn/logs
intention: A root's .artifact-journal.jsonl holds one line per record path, that path's newest entry, so it grows only with the record set. Every entry the door writes is also appended to a trail of one file per UTC day under ~/.cairn/logs, which the existing logs sweep ages out at 30 days.
why: Akien, 16:47 UTC 2026-11-16, relayed verbatim by the orchestrator: "then how about this... the latest entry remains in cairn commons, and everything else broken into... per day? per week? inside of our .cairn/logs folder". The orchestrator chose per day and stopped the segment build. Measured 2026-11-15: the Dell push of cairn/.artifact-journal.jsonl was 50.04 MB and GitHub warned GH001; the hard refusal is at 100 MB. Measured 2026-11-16: the commons journal is 55 MB and grows about 3 MB a day, so segments would only have moved the growth into more files in git.
traces_to: Law 5: the address carries what a mind needs now, and the trail past that berths outside the working surface while staying greppable. Law 7: a record of truth that cannot be pushed is lost off the box. Law 4: the bound is kept by the writing door, not by remembering to trim.
how: The index line for a path is that path's newest entry, verbatim. Each entry carries entry = sha256 of its own body (the existing _entry_sha). A new entry carries no prev; a migrated entry keeps the prev it had, as an inert field. A write takes the door lock, reads the index, drops the lines for its path, appends the new line, and replaces the file atomically. If the file changed between the read and the replace (a git rewrite that ignored the lock), the entry is parked and JournalLineOrphaned raises, as 0f8aefbba1d0 ruled; reland keeps working. The line order is write order, so the last line is still the newest write. After the index, the same entry is appended to log_path(operator, 0)/tools/artifact/journal/<root name>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl. Before any line leaves the index, it is appended to its own day file unless that file already holds it. A diagnostic world (set_diagnostic_roots or CAIRN_ARTIFACT_ROOTS) writes its trail to its own "trail" key, or beside its first root, never to the live logs. The trail is per box: it holds what this box's doors wrote, and history across boxes is the index's git history. verify_chain becomes verify_journal: each line parses, its entry hashes its body, and no path has two lines. The merge driver takes the union by path; the newer at wins, and a tie goes to the larger entry sha, so the result is the same in either order and is sorted by (at, path). A migrate door verb writes every line of a chained journal into its day file, then sets each past day file's mtime to the end of its day so the sweep ages it by its date. Then it writes the index. Re-running it adds nothing. A new read_trail(root) joins artifact's public interface for readers that need history.

outcomes.claim: after writes to two paths, one of them three times, the index holds exactly two lines, each that path's newest entry with its last line the newest write, and the trail day file for today holds all four entries verbatim

verify_journal returns no faults over a clean index, names the line when one byte of an entry is edited, and names the path when it has two lines; check_staged refuses the commit while either fault stands

on the index, check_staged refuses staged bytes that are not the newest sha_after, park_hand_edit restores the newest journaled bytes, and genesis journals only paths never journaled, so a hand-edited journaled record is not blessed and its commit is still refused

the merge driver over two indexes that each wrote the same path gives one line per path holding the newer entry, with a tie going to the larger entry sha, byte-identical in either order; a pre-migration side carrying many lines per path merges to its newest per path

no line leaves the index without standing in the trail: a write over an unmigrated journal puts that path's older lines in their own day files first, once; and a diagnostic world never writes the live logs trail

cairn artifact migrate <root> --why writes every line of a chained journal into the day file of its at, sets each past day file's mtime to the end of its day, and writes the newest-per-path index; a second run adds no trail line and changes no byte; a dry run on a scratch clone of each house repo is recorded in measured
